Management Plan
2026
European Personnel Selection Office
1

PART 1. Introduction
Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the Commission’s performance
management framework. The Commission’s strategic plan for 2025-2029 translates the
political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general objectives.
This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the actions of
all Commission services with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for 2025-
2029 in Management plan 2025. This outlook defines a set of multiannual objectives and
indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used for planning and
reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 management plan sets out what the European Personnel Selection Office (EPSO)
intends to deliver this year to contribute to these multiannual objectives (part 2) by fulfilling its
mission. It also describes how EPSO will contribute to the common objective of building a modern
and sustainable public administration (part 3). The main outputs with their indicators and targets
are presented in Annexes 1 and 2.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for EPSO.
Each specific objective is accompanied by one or two multiannual result indicators, one of
which is selected as a key performance indicator (KPI). The related outputs with their
indicators and targets are shown in Annexes 1 and 2 to this Plan.
3

PART 2. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities in 2026
Based on the above-listed specific objectives, EPSO has identified four key priorities.
These are illustrated below along with the related outputs:
The priorities in summary:
I) In 2026, EPSO will continue striving to improve its planning capacity. This will happen
through:
- An annual needs assessment exercise involving the collection of profiles sought by the EU
institutions to meet their future recruitment goals. After collection and assessment, EPSO will
translate those needs into a Competition Planning Proposal, for 2027 until mid-2028. The
planning proposal should reflect the top priorities of the EU institutions while taking into account
EPSO’s operational capacity.
- The main planning tool (Complan) developed under the Commission’s HRT Programme, which
includes functionalities enabling streamlined coordination of competitions as well as capacity
monitoring. EPSO will also finetune competition timelines, incorporating gains from EPSO’s new
test platform and HRT functionalities with the aim to progressively reduce competition duration.
Finally, EPSO will roll out the competition planning for 2026 as endorsed by its Management
Board.
II) Diversity and better candidate experience: EPSO continues enhancing its outreach
activities to promote EU Careers with the aim to increase the diversity of its candidate pool, by
increasing the total number of applicants, including from underrepresented EU Member States.
Furthermore, the Outreach and Communication Unit focuses on further enhancing the candidates’
4

experience by providing clear, transparent, and pro-active information to candidates during the
selection process. The Candidate Contact Service replies to queries and complaints in timely
manner. The candidates’ satisfaction is surveyed after the testing phase of each competition.
Outreach actions include participation in numerous online and in-person career events focusing
on underrepresented Member States, managing EPSO’s presence on 5 social media channels, as
well as coordinating EPSO’s flagship programmes for EU Careers Student and Staff Ambassadors.
III) The Commission’s Internal Audit Service (IAS) has delivered 5 recommendations (1) following
an audit to assess the adequacy of the governance, risk management and control processes set
up by EPSO when designing the new competition model. EPSO regards the audit as a strategic
opportunity for improvement and for addressing the reputational reservation included in the last
annual Activity Report particularly regarding reporting and performance indicators. EPSO has
developed the below Action Plan as well as a monitoring table to implement these
recommendations in 2026 and 2027. The actions foreseen under each recommendation feed
into this Management Plan.
(1) These are: (i) manage clients’ needs and communication aspects; (ii) set up a roadmap and a procedure
and carry out an impact analysis of the new competition model; (iii) define KPIs and monitor the
achievement of objectives of the new competition model; (iv) prepare EPSO for the use of artificial
intelligence; and (v) analyse lessons-learned.
5

IV) EPSO’s transformation process covers various sub-projects and has been ongoing for
several years. It is a complex exercise, and its implementation requires significant efforts in
change management, staff consultation, awareness-raising, training and monitoring. In 2026, it
needs to reach a consolidation phase. Key projects include the integration of the new test delivery
contractor, implementation of the new mid/long-term planning system and improving the
candidate experience (the latter two are mentioned above as standalone priorities). In addition, a
mission-critical priority is EPSO’s participation in the EC’s HRT project and replacing its outdated
IT infrastructure. Other projects worth mentioning include establishing a candidates’ anti-
cheating policy during online exams to preserve the integrity of competitions, consolidating the
internal workflows in support of the new competition model and enhance better coordinated
working methods in the Office. In 2025, the Board endorsed a proposal to launch a centralised
interinstitutional Job Market Portal under the EU Careers brand and this project is set to advance
in 2026. Finally, EPSO will is committed to embracing the AI revolution to improve concrete
processes. A dedicated AI@EPSO Workshop will prepare the ground for future initiatives.
Successfully addressing these priorities will enable EPSO to meet several key challenges that
will shape its operational context in 2026: onboarding successfully the new provider for online
test delivery to ensure technically sound and stable operations in the future; deploying the full
range of IT tools emanating from the HRT Programme thereby progressively replacing EPSO’s
outdated IT infrastructure; achieving a more reliable planning capacity and progressive shortening
of competition duration; organising the AD5 generalist competition after a 7-year interruption
and handling successfully a potentially unprecedented high volume of candidates; and attracting
more citizens from underrepresented Member States to apply for open competitions.
6

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable
levels through cost-effective controls. Failure to organise large-scale competitions is considered
a critical risk for which several mitigating measures have been taken.
EPSO has established an internal control system tailored to its particular characteristics and
circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will be assessed on an
ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to an annual assessment covering all
internal control principles.
A. Human resource management
In 2026, EPSO will continue to focus on the effective management of human resources in an
ongoing context of in-depth transformation, heavy workload and high expectations.
The main points of attention are:
1) Integration of the new test delivery provider(s): the onboarding process of the new
contractor(s) alongside the rollout of the new HRT tools requires significant involvement from
each Unit and team to ensure that the outcome meets the expectations. New and ongoing
competition also require diverse resources. Therefore, a flexible allocation of resources will
remain necessary to meet operational needs.
2) Gender and geographical balance: geographical balance being one of the political priorities
of the Commission, EPSO will also continue its effort in 2026 to improve the geo-balance
among its staff in order to better reflect the diversity of EU citizens, while keeping merit as
the primary recruitment criterion. 28% of EPSO current AD population come from an
underrepresented country.
3) Categories of staff: digitalisation, implementation of the new HRT tools and automatisation
of processes mean that jobs are progressively changing. In this context, EPSO will continue
to improve the balance between AD (increase in need of coordination skills) and AST staff
(decrease in logistical/technical jobs) so that the profiles evolve in an appropriate manner.
Further efficient measures should become possible once the benefits brought by the new
contractor(s) and the HRT tools can be precisely measured.
4) Flexibility, skills and competencies: in response to staff cuts and increased workload,
flexibility of the staff is a key element for a successful transition period. Therefore, EPSO
emphasizes developing in-house expertise and upgrading skills through tailored training
packages for effective onboarding and staff adaptation. In 2026, EPSO will promote cross-
team work and informal structures. It will maintain a 'Rapid Response Team' of versatile
7

colleagues to address peak workloads and unforeseen challenges through quick
redeployment, supporting internal redeployment effort necessary for operational continuity.
5) Staff engagement: EPSO will assess results of the most recent staff survey in 2026.
Management will continue to pay attention to the distribution of workload and promote a
healthy work/life balance in order to create appropriate conditions for fostering well-being
and mental health of staff. Regular interactive meetings with the Director will continue to
take place twice a month.
B. Digital transformation and data management
Digital transformation
EPSO will have a significant contribution in 2025 to several Digital Transformation strategic
objectives. EPSO is a member of the HR Transformation programme (HRT) of the Commission,
which aims to replace numerous legacy IT applications in the field of EU staff selection and
human resources with modern ones, increasing efficiency and usability. This will enable EPSO to
advance one of its mandatory indicators, the ‘Seamless digital environment (60% in 2025 to
90% in 2026): cloud adoption’ as the new tools are utilising mainly cloud infrastructure (where
the recommendations of the Cloud Council are followed and there are targets for continuous
improvement of the security posture) and replace IT legacy solutions. EPSO is a front-runner
amongst the members of the HR family to manage and run, since January 2025, open
competitions using the new tools. This contributes also to the ‘Business-driven digital
transformation’ as business processes are reconsidered with the aim to be automatised in the
new IT Tools, cross DG collaboration and interoperability are key components of the programme
as well as data openness through the implementation of a common HRT family database for the
applications of the HRT Program.
Regarding ‘Digital Culture’, EPSO is actively promoting IT training courses for its staff as well as
courses on how to use the new EPSO IT tools. It is mandatory for EPSO staff to follow at least
one IT or cybersecurity training course. This has already increased the percentage of EPSO
statutory staff that has completed at least one IT training course to 100% in 2025, which we
aim to maintain for 2026. . EPSO also adheres to the implementation of the actions outlined in
the EC Cybersecurity Strategy for 2025-2026 by reviewing, implementing and monitoring the
recommendations and remarks received in the periodic IT security reports it receives
EPSO is also contributing to the objective of the “Green, secure and resilient infrastructure”.
Data management
On data governance, our work is inherited from the HRT framework and for data analysis, a data
analyst has provided support to EPSO Units. For 2026, regarding data governance, the roadmap
remains inherited from the HRT programme. We specifically foresee work on the data catalogue.
We will also work on data asset ownership and definitions.
In terms of data quality, we will be working on the following in 2026:
8

• Regarding the data catalogue (OvalEdge), we intend to increase the number of data
assets definitions we work on by 50%.
• For data ownership and stewardship, we will keep on working on defining ownerships,
specifically with assets related with the HR Transformation programme. The target is
also to get to a 50% increase of managed assets.
Regarding data skills, the current data manager will keep on developing a network of
colleagues that can work on data governance, hence sharing what data governance. In addition
to this, the data manager will deliver 2 tailor-made trainings: (1) one on data analysis and (2)
one on automation.
Data protection
EPSO will continue to strive for full compliance with the Data protection Regulation (EU)
2018/1725, in particular while procuring and onboarding new contractors for online testing. Data
privacy records will be updated and reviewed as necessary.
C. Sound financial management
In 2026, EPSO budget amounts to €29.39 M (DB2026 at the time of drafting), entirely under
Heading VII of the EU budget – Administrative Expenditure. Close to 76% of this amount is co-
delegated to PMO, OIB/OIL, HR and DG DIGIT, who manage EPSO’s payroll, buildings, security and
IT systems. EPSO will directly manage €7.12 M, including the budget of EuSA (€2.8 M).
EPSO operating budget is dedicated to the organisation of open competitions and selection
procedures, through framework contracts for the development and delivery of tests and outreach
actions. Ex-post controls carried out in EPSO by DG HR are based on a random sample approach.
Ex-ante controls are done following the financial circuits in place (partially decentralised with
counterweight), which have been agreed with DG HR, with whom EPSO has a Service Level
Agreement on the provision of financial, procurement and internal control services.
EPSO will continue implementing its budget in the most efficient way, always looking to maximise
the use of the 2026 allocation. The main indicator chosen will be that the estimated risk at
payment remains below 2% of the expenditures, as in 2025.
The performance tables can be found in the annex 2 of this document.
9

D. Fraud risk management
EPSO is aiming at implementing the actions under its domain (selection through the organisation
of competitions) in the framework of the Commission’s anti-fraud strategy (CAFS) adopted in
2023.
Revision of EPSO’s Anti-Fraud Strategy (AFS) was launched in spring 2025, incorporating advice
received from OLAF. It is expected to submit it to the peer review in the course of January 2026
for an adoption of the final version, in the first quarter of 2026. It should be noted that EPSO
only manages administrative credits and while zero risk is impossible, the risk of fraud with a
direct financial impact for the EU budget remains very low. Nevertheless, EPSO is mindful of the
consequences a fraud could have on its reputation and gives it careful consideration in the
document.
With the update of the AFS, EPSO will increase its awareness raising efforts about aspects such
as conflicts of interests, leaking of confidential information, how to report fraud, about potential
new vulnerabilities, such as those arising from artificial intelligence or cyberthreats.
The performance tables can be found in the annex 2 of this document.
E. Sound environmental management
EPSO will continue to encourage its staff to adopt eco-friendly habits in their daily life, both at
the office and at home. In addition, EPSO will maintain its efforts to raise awareness among
colleagues by promoting participation in workshops and training sessions to explore ways in
which staff activities can enhance climate action efforts.
Continued and regular communications through internal social media, emails, will permit staff to
remain informed and motivated
The baseline established for EPSO emissions related to business travel was 539 tonnes of CO2
in 2019. EPSO aims to significantly continue to cut emissions from staff professional travels by
at least 50%, as announced in the Greening the European Commission Communication and action
plan (2022). This will be achieved by participating in fairs and conferences remotely and holding
EU Careers events online. This performance will be measure thanks to MiPS+.
